title: Local Vault
summary: An offline-first personal document vault that minimizes collection and keeps decryption keys on the user device.
intended_users: People storing sensitive household records on shared or intermittently connected devices.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: Searchable sync normally exposes document text or a reusable server-side key.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: Server-side indexing was rejected for confidentiality. Fully peer-to-peer sync was rejected because background delivery is unreliable on target mobile browsers.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Use local indexing and encrypted blob sync with explicit metadata minimization.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: Recovery is harder and cross-device search indexing is recomputed after enrollment.
design_decisions.validation_approach: Property tests cover ciphertext round trips, sync metadata allowlists, deletion retention, and corrupted envelopes.
design_decisions.reconsideration_conditions: Reconsider if platform secure storage is unavailable or encrypted-search research becomes deployable without server plaintext.

testing_strategy: Vitest property and boundary tests exercise encryption envelopes, metadata allowlists, conflict resolution, deletion tombstones, and malformed inputs. Runtime cryptography and browser secure-storage behavior remain unverified by Finch.
security_threat: A breached sync service attempts to recover document contents or correlate sensitive titles. Document bodies, titles, and search terms are encrypted locally; uploaded metadata is allowlisted and padded. Recovery material never reaches the service. Residual risk: Traffic timing and account-level blob counts remain observable.
production_limitation: Large vaults rebuild the local index slowly on a new device and background sync depends on browser scheduling.
technical_debt: Replace the in-memory version-vector adapter with a durable transactional queue and complete an external cryptography review.
track_alignment_explanation: Privacy is the product purpose: data minimization, local processing, user-held keys, bounded retention, and explicit residual metadata risks are central to the architecture.
